Project.Name: network-access.xml
Project.Title: Network & Access Modernization: Naming Plane, Governed Transport and Edge Enforcement

Task.Name: Phase 0 — Charter, alignment and inventory
N0.1 Naming-plane owner confirmed; pilot population defined; remote-access paths and residual VPN use inventoried
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsor and CIO Source: ../books/b09-network/09-who-owns-the-network.md#the-charters-plan-in-one-table

Task.Name: N0.2 AD DNS and DHCP inventory, read-only, committed as JSON; DnsAdmins emptied of non-domain-administrators
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: AD administrators Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-1-inventory-and-baseline

Task.Name: N0.3 DDI candidates scored on evidence: Marketplace status, policy-plane coverage, the five decisions, vendor questions in writing
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/12-selection-cost-and-residual-risk.md#selection-criteria

Task.Name: D-N1 DDI platform model
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsor and CIO Options: SaaS policy plane; agency-operated DDI inside the boundary; cloud-native services managed as code (enough on its own for a single-cloud agency with no divisional delegation) If decided late: Coexistence can't be deployed, and the pilot division's DNS move (program P2.6) has nothing to move onto Source: ../books/b08-ddi/12-selection-cost-and-residual-risk.md#comparing-the-platform-models

Task.Name: NG0 Gate 0 — Inventory committed and decisions owned
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Criteria: AD DNS inventory dated, committed and reviewed (Decision 4); every branch's redirect-dns target read from the running configuration; platform model decided; one named decider for every row of the DNS and network matrices Source: ../books/b08-ddi/08-reference-architecture.md#decision-4-ad-dns-inventory-before-retirement

Task.Name: Phase 1 — Naming and addressing
X-P17 Cloud DNS Private Resolver deployed (program P1.7)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: Coexistence has no cloud resolver to forward to, and Phase 1 waits Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N1.1 Coexistence: DDI resolvers deployed, Microsoft DNS and DHCP synchronized read-only, forwarding both ways with one path per namespace
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-2-deploy-coexistence

Task.Name: X-P26S Program starts the pilot division's DNS move (start of P2.6)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: The pilot division's zones and scopes have no coexistence to move through, and the program's pilot slips Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: D-N2 Resolver path: the redirect-dns target and the forwarding chain order (Decisions 1 and 2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Options: A DDI resolver at the branch; a forwarding proxy in a regional hub. Never a client loopback stub, and any SASE resolver is a forwarding target of the agency resolver, never the redirect target If decided late: Branch edges can't be retargeted; Protective DNS, logging and response policy stay off the branch path Source: ../books/b08-ddi/08-reference-architecture.md#decision-1-the-redirect-dns-destination

Task.Name: N1.2 Edge retargeted: redirect-dns to agency resolvers, SASE DNS as a forwarding target, order verified in the running configuration
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#retargeting-the-edge

Task.Name: D-N3 Order of zones to move, and the cutover pattern for each
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Options: Per zone: split horizon, subdomain delegation, or progressive migration with conditional forwarding. AD locator records stay where domain controllers can register them, and move last If decided late: Authority can't move zone by zone; the pilot division's zones wait Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#three-cutover-patterns

Task.Name: X-P26 Pilot division's DNS migrated and DHCP re-homed (program P2.6)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: The cutover loop hasn't been proven on a division, so the remaining zone moves wait Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N1.3 Non-AD zones, forwarders, GlobalNames and reverse zones moved through the cutover loop
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#zones-and-records

Task.Name: N1.4 Clients and DHCP scopes moved in waves with the program's divisions (option 6, VNet DNS settings)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#moving-clients-in-waves

Task.Name: N1.5 Cloud federation: IPAM federation, private endpoint zones published once, validation matrix run from every origin
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Cloud platform teams Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-4-cloud-federation

Task.Name: NG1 Gate 1 — Naming plane authoritative for the pilot scope
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Criteria: Every name class in the validation matrix resolves correctly from on-premises, each cloud and the branch path; no private endpoint name returns a public address; OCSP and CRL endpoints resolve from every origin; every branch's redirect-dns target is an agency resolver; resolution-path consistency baselined Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-4-cloud-federation

Task.Name: Phase 2 — Securing the governor
D-N4 Control-plane hosting model, recorded as the boundary disposition
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsor and CIO Options: An on-premises control plane; Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN for Government, cloud-hosted and FedRAMP Certified at Class C (Moderate). A hosted controller doesn't remove the directive's obligations If decided late: The control plane can't be built or hardened, and the pilot waits Source: ../books/b09-network/11-field-office-wan-transformation.md#risks-and-mitigations

Task.Name: N2.1 Control plane built and taken through the ED 26-03 sequence: inventory, off-box logs, patch, hunt, harden, syslog to CISA through CLAW
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/05-sd-wan-sase-and-governed-transport.md#securing-the-controller-and-the-edges

Task.Name: N2.2 Pilot circuits bought on measured physics: per-site latency and loss recorded, diversity, static addressing confirmed with carriers
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/13-sequencing-cost-and-evidence.md#the-decision-sequence

Task.Name: N2.3 Boundary change and branch use-case package prepared as a significant change, with the evidence the authorization package needs
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: System owner Source: ../books/b09-network/13-sequencing-cost-and-evidence.md#evidence-for-the-boundary-change

Task.Name: NG2 Gate 2 — Governor secured before it carries traffic
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO and ISSO Criteria: Controller and edges under vulnerability management on BOD 26-04 windows, privileged-access control and off-box logging; every edge in the fleet inventory with its software version and support date; an ED 26-03-style inventory, log collection and patch sequence executable within a day; SD-WAN syslog reaching CISA through CLAW Source: ../books/b09-network/08-reference-architecture.md#decision-4-bring-the-governor-under-control-before-it-carries-traffic

Task.Name: Phase 3 — Identity-driven access pilot
N3.1 Identity claims reachable by every access decision point; gaps listed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/09-who-owns-the-network.md#the-charters-plan-in-one-table

Task.Name: N3.2 Application-to-path routing policy (the SC-7(4) traffic-flow policy), site register and architecture review determination
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: System owner Source: ../books/b09-network/12-microsoft-365-traffic.md#the-three-instruments

Task.Name: D-N5 Egress pattern for each pilot site
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Options: A, hairpin; C, governed local breakout (the program's reference pattern); D, agent-delivered SASE. Never B, bare local breakout If decided late: Pilot sites can't be built, and the boundary change can't name its enforcement points Source: ../books/b09-network/08-reference-architecture.md#decision-3-choose-the-egress-pattern-per-site-and-change-the-boundary-first

Task.Name: D-N6 Path to a domain controller for each branch class
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Options: A private path (MPLS, IPsec or the SD-WAN overlay); a ZTNA connector that publishes the domain controllers (single sign-on only); a Kerberos KDC proxy If decided late: Pilot branches on local breakout lose sign-in, Group Policy and password change while cloud applications keep working Source: ../books/b09-network/06-legacy-protocols-on-re-routed-paths.md#ways-to-provide-the-path

Task.Name: N3.3 Ten pilot sites built: edges, regional breakout, security service edge, deterministic egress, a monitored path to a domain controller
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/11-field-office-wan-transformation.md#implementation-roadmap

Task.Name: D-N7 Boundary change for local egress, decided before the first production cutover
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Authorizing official Options: Approve the significant change through reauthorization or ongoing authorization; refuse, and the sites stay on their current path If decided late: No production cutover can start: the boundary change comes first Source: ../books/b09-network/13-sequencing-cost-and-evidence.md#the-decision-sequence

Task.Name: D-N8 Microsoft 365 Optimize exemption (the SC-7(4) traffic-flow exception)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Authorizing official Options: Grant it for a stated duration and review cadence, on named and compensating controls; refuse it If decided late: Optimize traffic stays on the inspected path at the pilot sites, and the cutover waits Source: ../books/b09-network/12-microsoft-365-traffic.md#the-sc-74-documented-traffic-flow-exception

Task.Name: D-N9 Fabric go-live, site by site: governor live, inspecting and logging
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: System owner Options: Turn on the site's new egress; hold the site on its current path If decided late: Pilot traffic stays on the old path, and the 30-day stability clock doesn't start Source: ../books/b09-network/09-who-owns-the-network.md#an-owner-for-each-step

Task.Name: N3.4 Pilot cutover; 30 stable days; CISA telemetry parity confirmed per site; one path decision emitted as a claim
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/05-sd-wan-sase-and-governed-transport.md#the-evidence-the-fabric-must-emit

Task.Name: NG3 Gate 3 — Pilot governed and evidenced
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Pilot sites stable for 30 days with the control layer live, inspecting and logging to the SIEM; boundary change decided before cutover; SC-7(4) memo signed and site register current; CISA telemetry parity confirmed per site before any legacy circuit ends; one path decision emitted as a claim; the VPN path documented as residual Source: ../books/b09-network/09-who-owns-the-network.md#an-owner-for-each-step

Task.Name: Phase 4 — Customer-edge enforcement
D-N10 RADIUS and NAC platform, and the trigger that retires NPS (D3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsor and CIO Options: NPS through the hybrid-joined phase only; an on-premises NAC platform reading Intune compliance; a cloud-delivered NAC or RADIUS service with the right FedRAMP authorization; VPN or ZTNA federated to Entra ID for remote access If decided late: Enforcement can't be designed, and Entra-joined devices can't be admitted before cloud-native cutover removes the AD objects NPS relies on Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#what-can-replace-it

Task.Name: X-P27 Cloud PKI certificates issued; Wi-Fi and VPN verified (program P2.7)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: Monitor mode has no device certificates to authenticate, and the NAC rollout waits Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N4.1 NAC platform registered for Intune compliance retrieval; policy tiers built; monitor mode on pilot ports with a baseline report
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#posture-comes-from-intune-not-from-a-probe

Task.Name: D-N11 Move the pilot sites from monitor mode to wired enforcement
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Options: Enforce on workstation ports; stay in monitor mode until the baseline's exceptions are closed If decided late: Wired and wireless enforcement wait, and devices are still admitted before they authenticate Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#rolling-it-out

Task.Name: N4.2 Wired enforcement: open mode removed, CoA tested, captive portal up, IoT devices registered in IPAM, detections routed to the SOC
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#rolling-it-out

Task.Name: N4.3 Wireless enforcement on WPA3-Enterprise, then IoT segmentation and a rogue-device tabletop
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#rolling-it-out

Task.Name: NG4 Gate 4 — Customer edge enforced for the pilot
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO and ISSO Criteria: Monitor-mode baseline report filed; wired and wireless enforcement live at the pilot sites; the three minimum detections alerting the SOC; RADIUS accounting, Intune compliance reports and DHCP audit logs kept for assessors; every MAB exception dated Source: ../books/b09-network/07-network-access-control.md#inventory-profiling-and-logs

Task.Name: Phase 5 — AD DNS and DHCP decommission
X-P43 AD-integrated zones moved, except the domain's own (program P4.3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: The 30-day SRV hold and the decommission gates can't start Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: N5.1 SRV hold: every critical locator record resolves from every VNet and site, every 15 minutes, for 30 clean days
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/11-operating-the-control-plane.md#srv-record-monitoring

Task.Name: N5.2 Inventory reconciled both ways; failover tested on the new resolvers and DHCP; query logs show the old servers idle
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-5-decommission-ad-dns-and-dhcp

Task.Name: N5.3 Hardening: Protective DNS forwarding, encrypted DNS, DNSSEC signing and validation where required, monitoring dashboards
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-6-policy-and-compliance-hardening

Task.Name: D-N12 Decommission AD DNS and Windows DHCP
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Sponsor and CIO Options: Decommission once all five gates pass, including 90 days of parallel operation; hold the legacy servers. Never on a date alone If decided late: Legacy DNS servers and their DnsAdmins exposure stay in service into the program's AD retirement phase Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-5-decommission-ad-dns-and-dhcp

Task.Name: N5.4 Legacy DNS servers retired in order; exports archived; records officer confirms disposition; 7-day burn-in
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: AD administrators Source: ../books/b08-ddi/10-migration-sequence.md#phase-5-decommission-ad-dns-and-dhcp

Task.Name: NG5 Gate 5 — Legacy name services retired, evidence complete
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: DNS/DDI team Criteria: Gates 3 and 4 passed; Chapter 11's evidence checklist complete, the five decisions checked first; no client impact through the burn-in; logs searchable for six months and retrievable for a year; DnsAdmins and delegated roles reviewed; only the domain's own zones left on AD DNS, reached by forwarding, until the last domain controllers go Source: ../books/b08-ddi/11-operating-the-control-plane.md#sample-evidence-checklist
